entities.summary: John David Souther was an American singer, songwriter, and actor. He was "a principal architect of the Southern California sound and a major influence on a generation of songwriters". Souther wrote and co-wrote songs recorded by Linda Ronstadt and some of the Eagles' biggest hits, including "Best of My Love", "Victim of Love", "Heartache Tonight" and "New Kid in Town". "How Long", which appeared on the Eagles' Long Road Out of Eden, came from Souther's first solo album. He recorded two hit songs in his solo career: "You're Only Lonely" (1979) and "Her Town Too" (1981), a duet with James Taylor.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a songwriter and musician, J.D. Souther's contributions to the Southern California sound influenced a generation of songwriters, including Linda Ronstadt and the Eagles, who recorded numerous hits that remain iconic in American music.
